findings.obligation: E3: a run whose store write failed never shows a repos-read count that claims more repos were read than the store actually holds for that run.
findings.observation: then_her_queue_counts_exactly asserts text.contains("{n} repos read"), a substring test with no boundary. A displayed over-count whose decimal text ends in the true count satisfies it: with 5 repos read, a queue rendering '15 repos read' contains '5 repos read' and the assertion passes. The direction E3 names explicitly - claiming MORE repos read than the store holds - is exactly the direction this hole is open in. The in-scope untrue zero ('0 repos read') and any under-count still fail correctly, so the falsifier is weakened, not absent.
findings.remediation: Read the count out of the queue's status line and assert equality with repos.len() (an exact captured number, or at minimum a boundary-anchored match of the whole status line), keeping the existing WHAT/WHY/HOW message.

findings.obligation: E2: an interrupted scan can be run again and resumes that run, instead of forcing the user to abandon it and start over.
findings.observation: when_she_resumes asserts offers("Resume scan") and then delegates to when_scan_finishes (support/review_app/world.rs:292-296), which presses the FIRST label present among ["Scan my repos", "Scan again", "Resume scan"]. The step never presses RESUME_SCAN itself and never asserts the other two labels are absent at the resume moment (the earlier THEN asserts only that 'Scan again' is absent, on the queue page it opened before the restart). If the interrupted queue also offers 'Scan my repos', the scenario starts a fresh run and still satisfies every remaining assertion, so the observation cannot distinguish resuming from starting over - the user-visible half of E2 that the acceptance disposition did NOT trade away.
findings.remediation: In when_she_resumes press RESUME_SCAN explicitly (browser.try_press(RESUME_SCAN)) before polling /scan/status, or assert that no fresh-scan label is offered alongside it, so the completed run that the count is then read from is provably the resumed one.

findings.obligation: Reuse closure: reuse an existing support helper that already owns the same step instead of duplicating it.
findings.observation: when_she_scans is a byte-for-byte duplicate of the existing public step review_app::repos_and_accounts::when_scans (support/review_app/repos_and_accounts.rs:1041-1045): same mark, same when_scan_finishes, same repos_read_since tuple. Two homes for one step, which drift independently the moment either changes.
findings.remediation: Delete when_she_scans and call the existing when_scans in both scenarios (it is already in scope through review_app::repos_and_accounts), keeping the scenario bodies' visible step composition unchanged.

findings.obligation: E1: when a scan cannot write its results to the store, the run ends Interrupted and never reports itself as Completed - the promised outcome must be observed failing for its own reason, not only the absence of its test seam.
findings.observation: The recorded RED is the development build refusing the fault name at startup (review_app_scan_store_failure.rs:85), so then_the_scan_ended_interrupted, the queue's absent-count assertions and then_her_queue_counts_exactly have never executed. Nothing on record shows they can fail; the designer's scratch-case report is uncommitted and uncorroborated.
findings.remediation: Within this slice, after config.rs accepts the two fault names and the store refuses the write, but BEFORE scan.rs stops discarding the mark_repo_read / record_account_checks errors, run 'cargo test -p openlore-review-app --test review_app_scan_store_failure' once and keep the output showing the failure has moved to then_the_scan_ended_interrupted (status "completed"); only then make it GREEN. If the intermediate state is not reachable, say so with the reason instead of skipping the observation.

observations.text: Selection (mechanical, this review). Project test-impact tooling first, twice, and it decided nothing either time: (a) 'code-fact impacted-tests tests/acceptance/review_app_scan_store_failure.rs --root .' ran past 120 s, stdout and stderr EMPTY, pipeline exit 0 - an empty selection; (b) after S2's production commit, 'code-fact impacted-tests crates/adapter-review-store/src/scan_runs.rs crates/review-domain/src/views/queue.rs crates/ports/src/review.rs --root .' produced 0 bytes for about four minutes and I terminated it (exit 143, SIGTERM, no output), so no selection was obtained for the changed production paths either. Fell back to the repository's own change set. Against the slice base: 'git diff --name-only 16ad353 3fa912a -- tests/ crates/' gives crates/openlore-review-app/Cargo.toml, tests/acceptance/review_app_legacy_run_repos_read.rs, tests/acceptance/review_app_scan_store_failure.rs, tests/acceptance/support/review_app/app.rs plus S2's four production files. S1 scope keeps the declared oracle and its two declared supports (Cargo.toml, support/review_app/app.rs); review_app_legacy_run_repos_read.rs is S2's oracle and was left to its own reviewer, and S2's production files are read-only here. The selected test is the slice's declared verification command, run in R2. Because the tool answered nothing, the selection rests on the change set, not on a dependency analysis: any test reaching the S1 oracle's dependencies that this change set does not name would be unselected, which is an explicit limit of this selection.

Run (my own execution, clean HEAD 3fa912a, 'git status --porcelain' empty): argv 'cargo test -p openlore-review-app --test review_app_scan_store_failure', cwd /Users/jeffbailey/Projects/foss/leading/openlore, exit 101. stdout: 'Compiling openlore-review-app v0.0.1', 'Finished test profile in 4.46s', 'running 4 tests'; 2 passed (the state_delta support self-tests compiled into the suite); 2 failed - a_scan_that_cannot_save_her_account_checks_is_offered_for_resuming and a_scan_that_cannot_save_that_it_read_a_repo_is_offered_for_resuming; 'test result: FAILED. 2 passed; 2 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 2.35s'; stderr beyond that only cargo's own 'error: test failed, to rerun pass -p openlore-review-app --test review_app_scan_store_failure'. Both panics at review_app_scan_store_failure.rs:85:49 (the GIVEN step), each carrying the app's own startup log {"event":"health.startup.refused","probe":"config","reason":"REVIEW_APP_TEST_FAULT is invalid: not a known test fault"}, exit Some(2), for "refuse_record_account_checks" and "refuse_mark_repo_read" respectively. Output kept at /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-jeffbailey-Projects-foss-leading-openlore/2e5be832-19d9-47f2-b3d4-a99c5d91a0cd/scratchpad/s1-red-reviewer-3fa912a.txt. Same observation as my earlier run at ef5f6e5 (exit 101, same two failures, same reason, 2.63s), which is cited only as a prior execution, never restamped.

RED classification at 3fa912a: semantic, not BROKEN. The suite compiled (the review-app crate rebuilt after S2's commit, 'Finished test profile in 4.46s'), the support module resolved, the real app binary built and launched, and the process that refused is the app's own config probe rejecting a fault name the S1 design declares as new production behaviour of crates/openlore-review-app/src/config.rs (precedent migrate_before_commit, already accepted by that same module and already driven by review_app_repos_and_accounts.rs). So the failure is absent declared production behaviour reached through the oracle's declared seam, not an import error, a nonexistent fixture, a cross-root path mismatch or a fixture-caused provider mismatch; no oracle-side infrastructure defect is implicated. The panic message states WHAT (the build refused the asked fault), WHY (nothing can then show the owner the honest outcome) and HOW (accept the name on the development fault seam, make that one store write error on every call, keep the release build refusing it and the release binary free of the names).

Closure, both directions, against E1/E2/E3 and P1. E1 (ends Interrupted, never reports Completed): falsified by then_the_scan_ended_interrupted (assert_eq status == "interrupted", status read from the public /scan/status endpoint after polling out of 'running') and by the '!page.offers("Scan again")' assertion on the queue. E2 (resumable, not forced to start over): falsified by the two 'offers("Resume scan")' assertions (the queue after the cut-short run, and again at the resume step) plus then_the_scan_ended_completed on the restarted store; the frozen-plan identity of the resumed run is explicitly dispositioned out in acceptance.md S1 as a separate promise already observed elsewhere. E3 (never an untrue repos-read count): falsified by the negative text assertions over both wordings ('repos read' / 'repo read') on the interrupted queue, and by then_her_queue_counts_exactly comparing the queue's count against repos_read_since, an independent oracle built from the GitHub double's request log rather than from the store rows the production count is computed from. No oracle observation lacks a declared promise: every assertion serves P1's interrupted / resumable / truthful-count outcome. Both refused writes named by the design (mark_repo_read, record_account_checks) have one scenario each, driven only through the public HTTP port, /scan/status and the queue page; the store, sign-in, ownership proof and scan are real, only GitHub and ATProto are doubled.

What the recorded RED does NOT yet establish: at both executed revisions both scenarios die in the GIVEN, so no business assertion of P1 has ever been reached, let alone seen failing for its own reason. The designer's report that the interrupted/resume/count steps were exercised against unchanged production in an uncommitted scratch case is uncorroborated by any evidence in this review and is not treated as observed. The semantic RED on record is therefore 'the declared fault seam does not exist', a true missing-production-behaviour RED at a declared S1 target but a weaker witness than 'the scan reports Completed when its store write was refused'. Kept as a completion obligation in the finding owned by implementation; it does not block craft, because the only way to observe the stronger RED is to land the seam first.

Supports and constructibility. The declared support delta (against slice base 16ad353) is additive only: app.rs gains 'pub const TEST_FAULT_VAR' (line 42), 'restart_without_test_fault' (line 401, retains extra_env minus that var, then restart()) and one doc-table row; Cargo.toml gains the two [[test]] targets. No existing call site changes, so no other review_app_* suite is affected and none was selected. Every helper the oracle leans on already exists and compiles: ReviewWorld::launch (world.rs:109, two closures), Startup::Refused { exit_code, logs } (app.rs:69), given_github_verified, when_scan_finishes (world.rs:292), github_mark / repos_read_since (repos_and_accounts.rs:1015/1020), Page::offers (browser.rs:71). Constructibility is proved by the run itself: the suite built and executed at 3fa912a. Test time: not measurable before the seam exists (the whole suite exits in 2.35s on the refusal); the design states no per-test budget and no derogation, and these app-launch scenarios follow the incumbent review-app acceptance convention, so no timing receipt is owed at this phase. Capability limit: typesafe unavailable - 'python jev_decide.py --request <file> --output -' exit 3, 'TYPESAFE_API_KEY is absent from this process environment' (invoked from a shell command, not a tool kernel); the five classification questions I had batched (E1/E2/E3 closure, RED attribution, whether the business RED was reached) were decided locally from the bytes and the runs instead.

Commit comparison, ef5f6e5 (the revision the oracle was committed on) to the reviewed clean HEAD 3fa912a. 'git log --oneline ef5f6e5..HEAD' is two commits: 8607f19 'docs: the S2 repos-read oracle is accepted, with its measured RED' and 3fa912a 'fix(review-app): a run kept before scan plans shows no repos-read line'. 'git diff --name-only ef5f6e5 HEAD' is crates/adapter-review-store/src/scan_runs.rs, crates/ports/src/review.rs, crates/review-domain/src/views/queue.rs, crates/review-domain/tests/page_contracts.rs and the two S2 run records. 'git diff --stat ef5f6e5 HEAD -- tests/acceptance/review_app_scan_store_failure.rs tests/acceptance/support/ crates/openlore-review-app/Cargo.toml crates/openlore-review-app/src/ Cargo.lock rust-toolchain.toml' is EMPTY: the S1 oracle, both declared supports, the whole review-app crate (config.rs and scan.rs included) and the toolchain/lock pins are byte-identical to the bytes I first read and ran. S2's commit did change production the S1 oracle reads through - the queue page renderer, the scan-run store adapter and its port - so equivalence of relevant inputs was NOT established and the affected check was RERUN rather than reused: the run recorded in R2 is a fresh execution on 3fa912a, and its result is unchanged. No S2 record was touched.

diagnostic: APPROVED for craft, on clean HEAD 3fa912a. The oracle is public, independent and constructible: both scenarios drive the real app process through its HTTP driving port, /scan/status and the queue page, with the real store and only GitHub and ATProto doubled, and they build and execute (R2, a fresh run at 3fa912a; S2's production commit changed inputs the oracle reads, so the affected check was rerun, not reused - R7). Closure holds both ways: E1 by the strict 'interrupted' status plus the absent 'Scan again', E2 by the two 'Resume scan' offers plus the completed resumed run, E3 by the negative count assertions and by a count compared against an independent oracle (the GitHub double's request log, not the store rows production counts); no assertion serves a promise that was not declared. The measured RED is semantic, not BROKEN: the app's own config probe refuses refuse_mark_repo_read / refuse_record_account_checks, declared S1 behaviour of the declared target crates/openlore-review-app/src/config.rs, with build, supports, imports and runtime all sound and a panic that states WHAT/WHY/HOW. Four findings, none blocking craft: three owned by oracle (a boundary-less substring count assertion that an over-count can satisfy; a resume step whose press goes through a helper that may press a fresh-scan label instead of 'Resume scan'; a step duplicating the existing support helper when_scans) and one owned by implementation (observe the business RED on then_the_scan_ended_interrupted once the seam lands and before scan.rs is fixed, since no business assertion of P1 has yet executed). Capability limits retained: typesafe unavailable (TYPESAFE_API_KEY absent, exit 3), and the project's test-impact tool returned no selection on either attempt, so selection rests on the repository change set since the slice base. Implementation GREEN on both scenarios and the three oracle findings remain completion obligations.
